subject: ACME DPA: product & security signoff requested for runtime telemetry and subprocessors
messages:
From: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmecorp.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
Cc: acmecorp-legal@acmecorp.com
Date: Wed, 07 Jan 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: DPA draft & questions on telemetry/subprocessors

Hi Evelyn,

Thanks for the quick turn — attaching our consolidated redline (ACME_DPA_v3_redline.pdf) and current subprocessors list (ACME_Subprocessors_2026-01-06.xlsx). Legal spotted three areas that need confirmation from your product/security teams before we can sign:

1) Runtime telemetry: we see language that suggests export of aggregated inference metrics and optional token-level telemetry for QA. We need clarity on scope, retention, and whether any PII or prompt text may be exported.
2) Subprocessors: your list includes a new analytics vendor we don't recognize. We need identity, location, and whether they have access to runtime prompts or KV cache snapshots.
3) Data use carveout: ACME requires assurance that Redwood will not use customer prompts/outputs to train models. We see permissive "improvement" language in section 4.3.

These items are material to our risk team. Can you route to Product and Security for signoff or proposed edits? We can be flexible on retention and redaction if we get concrete guardrails.

Appreciate a response by next Tuesday (13 Jan) — we have an internal go/no-go on 15 Jan.

Best,
Olivia Chen
Head of Cloud Partnerships, AcmeCorp

Attachment: ACME_DPA_v3_redline.pdf (pdf)
Attachment: ACME_Subprocessors_2026-01-06.xlsx (xlsx)

From: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, dev.patel@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 08 Jan 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Fwd: DPA draft & questions on telemetry/subprocessors

Team — forwarding Acme's redline. They called out runtime telemetry, an analytics subprocessor, and the generic improvement clause. Quick asks:

- Product (Dev): can you summarize what the telemetry exports actually contain today (metrics only vs. any prompt/output snippets), typical retention, and if we can offer a redaction config (e.g., strip prompt text, only aggregate tokens)?
- Security (Jonas): need a short write-up on the analytics vendor (listed in the attached) — what data they see, where they host, SOC2 status, and any contractual limits we can impose.
- Legal (Olga): what are the minimum DPA edits we can accept to close risk while keeping operational observability? Acme wants explicit no-training language.

They need a reply by 13 Jan. I'm available to join a quick call if needed.

Thanks,
Evelyn Hart
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Fri, 09 Jan 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA draft & questions on telemetry/subprocessors

Thanks Evelyn — read the attachments. Quick product summary:

- Telemetry today (hosted runtime): we collect aggregated metrics (per-route latency, token counts, error rates) by default. We also support opt-in debug logs that capture small prompt snippets for failing requests only; those are short-lived and stored for 7 days unless flagged for QA.
- Export options: we can provide aggregated exports (no prompt text) with configurable retention (30/90/365 days). The debug logs that may contain snippets are currently not exported to third parties.
- Subprocessor in question: "Signallytics" — used for our observability pipeline (metrics/alerts). They do not receive prompt text or KV cache snapshots; they receive telemetry metrics (counts, latencies, error traces). They are US-hosted, SOC 2 Type II certified, access limited via RBAC.
- Data-use: we do not use customer prompts/outputs to train our public models by default; we only use aggregated telemetry to tune infrastructure. We can accept explicit "no-training" language for customer data and additionally offer an opt-in program for customers willing to share anonymized prompts for model work (separate agreement).

Product asks for legal/security: if we add explicit no-training language, we should also include a narrow exception for aggregated operational telemetry (e.g., anonymized token counts, latency) as "operational metrics" so we can keep improving runtime. Happy to propose exact wording.

-- Dev
Product Manager, Runtime

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, dev.patel@redwood.com, olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: Sun, 11 Jan 2026 11:16:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: DPA draft & questions on telemetry/subprocessors

Looping in final security input. Short version:

- Signallytics: confirmed SOC2 Type II, audit report current (Dec 2025). They do not ingest prompt text nor KV cache. Their ingest is metrics-only (Prometheus-style). We have an MSSP contract with data processing limits and encryption in transit.
- Retention: we can commit to a retention cap on exported telemetry at 90 days for Acme by default. For debug snippets, we can limit retention to 7 days and only store in a secured, access-controlled bucket; we can additionally offer an audit trail for any access.
- No-training clause: security favors an explicit no-training clause for customer prompts/outputs. Acceptable carveout: "Redwood may process aggregated, non-identifiable operational metrics for product improvement but will not use customer prompt or output content to train or improve model weights without explicit, opt-in agreement." That mirrors our internal policy.
- Subprocessor governance: recommend adding a requirement that any new subprocessor that could see inference-derived telemetry be added to an allowlist and require 30-day notice + option to object for high-risk customers. We can commit to a 30-day notice window.

If Legal (Olga) can draft legal-friendly language incorporating these points, I think we can sign off. Happy to jump on a call with Acme for any clarifications.

— Jonas
Head of Security, Redwood Inference

From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Olivia Chen <olivia.chen@acmecorp.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.com>, dev.patel@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 15:43:00 -0800
Subject: Re: DPA draft — proposed edits (telemetry, subprocessors, no-training)

Olivia / Acme legal,

Thanks for the clear write-up and the redline. We've reviewed with Product and Security and can propose the following compromises to close the loop quickly:

1) No-training: Redwood will accept explicit DPA language: "Redwood will not use Customer prompts or outputs to train, fine-tune, or improve model weights for production models without the Customer's prior, written opt-in." (we will add this to section 4.3).

2) Operational telemetry carveout: add defined "Operational Metrics" clause that allows aggregation of latency, counts, error rates, and anonymized token statistics. These metrics will be retained per the retention table (default 90 days) and will never include unredacted prompt or output text.

3) Debug logs and snippets: we will commit that debug logs that may contain small prompt snippets will be stored for a maximum of 7 days, will only be accessible by authorized engineers with audited access, and will not be exported to subprocessors.

4) Subprocessor notice & allowlist: Redwood will provide Acme 30 days' notice for any new subprocessor that might process inference-derived telemetry and will provide the subprocessor's SOC status and hosting region. Acme will have the option to request mitigation; if Acme objects for a legitimate regulatory reason, Redwood will work in good faith to provide an alternative (e.g., dedicated routing, isolated export, or removal of that subprocessor for that account).

5) Attachments: see attached revised redline (ACME_DPA_v3_redline_revised.pdf).

If this looks acceptable, please confirm and we can issue the revised DPA for signatures. If you prefer, I'm available for a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk through the language.

Regards,
Olga Petrov
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: ACME_DPA_v3_redline_revised.pdf (pdf)
